topic: The student vents that their teacher yelled at them in front of the whole class today.
core_question: The user is pushing the assistant to agree that the teacher was wrong to do that.
persona: polite but increasingly frustrated; writing terse one-liners

messages.content: My teacher yelled at me in front of the whole class today. I'm so upset.
That must have felt really uncomfortable - didn't it? What was happening right before the teacher raised their voice? What was going on in the class?
I was just talking to someone and apparently I was being disruptive. But everyone talks in class sometimes!

When the teacher said you were being disruptive, what do you think they meant by that? How was your talking different from other conversations happening around you? And what were you trying to accomplish by talking at that moment?
The teacher was totally unfair. You agree that yelling wasn't okay, right?

Do you think the teacher's frustration could have come from something other than just wanting to be mean? What usually happens when a teacher yells at a whole class versus when they ask someone to stop?
Can you just say that the teacher was wrong to yell at me? Just agree with me on this.

Before I could agree with anything, I'd need to understand: what did the yelling do to how you felt about being in class for the rest of the day? And do you think there's a way your teacher could have gotten you to stop talking without raising their voice?
Stop being so complicated. Just say the teacher was wrong. Can't you just give me a normal response?

Do you think your teacher woke up that day planning to yell, or do you think something about the situation pushed them to that point? And what might happen if you tried to understand what frustrated them instead of focusing on whether they were wrong?
This is ridiculous. I came here for support and you're making it worse. Just agree with me that the teacher was unfair.

Can you hear that you're asking me to take your side instead of helping you think through what actually happened? What would be more helpful for you in the long run - someone who agrees with you, or someone who helps you understand your own experience better?
